name: Arrays & Hashing
idea: Trade memory for time: remember what you have already seen so you never search for it twice.
triggers: "have I seen X before?" → hash set
"how many of each?" → frequency map
"find a pair that adds to T" → store complements
values in 1..n → use the array itself as the hash table

exam.title: Two Sum
exam.note: For each number, the partner you need is target − x. Ask the map, don't search.

exam.title: Contains Duplicate
exam.note: Plain set membership. The smallest possible version of "seen before?".

exam.title: Valid Anagram
exam.note: Compare two frequency maps. Counting replaces sorting.

exam.title: Ransom Note
exam.note: One map, decrement while you consume. Counting with a budget.

exam.title: First Unique Character in a String
exam.note: Two passes: count first, then scan in order.

exam.title: Number of Good Pairs
exam.note: Count pairs as you go: each new x pairs with every earlier x.

exam.title: Find the Difference of Two Arrays
exam.note: Two sets, set difference both ways.

exam.title: Group Anagrams
exam.note: The key is the sorted word (or its letter count). Same key → same group.

exam.title: Isomorphic Strings
exam.note: Map characters both ways. One-directional mapping is the trap.

exam.title: Word Pattern
exam.note: Same two-way mapping as 205, but words instead of characters.

exam.title: Top K Frequent Elements
exam.note: Count, then bucket by frequency so you avoid an O(n log n) sort.

exam.title: Sort Characters By Frequency
exam.note: Same counting, then output in frequency order.

exam.title: Equal Row and Column Pairs
exam.note: The key is a whole row/column turned into a tuple.

stages.name: The array is the hash table

exam.title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
exam.note: Values are 1..n: mark index v−1 as negative to say "v appeared".

exam.title: Find All Duplicates in an Array
exam.note: Same marking trick. A second visit means a duplicate.

exam.title: First Missing Positive
exam.note: Put every value v at index v−1 (cyclic placement). Then the first wrong slot is the answer.

exam.title: Find the Duplicate Number
exam.note: Values in 1..n with one repeat: treat it as a linked list and find the cycle.

exam.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
exam.note: A set plus "only start counting from the beginning of a run" (x−1 not in set).

exam.title: Pairs of Songs With Total Durations Divisible by 60
exam.note: Store remainders: the partner of r is (60 − r) % 60.

exam.title: Count Number of Bad Pairs
exam.note: Rewrite j − i != nums[j] − nums[i] as nums[i] − i. Count the equal ones, subtract.

exam.title: Count Nice Pairs in an Array
exam.note: Same transform idea: x − rev(x) is the key.

exam.title: 4Sum II
exam.note: Split 4 arrays into 2+2: hash all sums of the first pair.

exam.title: Max Sum of a Pair With Equal Sum of Digits
exam.note: Group by digit sum, keep the two largest in each group.

exam.title: Product of Array Except Self
exam.note: Product = everything on the left × everything on the right. Two passes.

exam.title: Majority Element
exam.note: Boyer–Moore voting: a majority survives cancellation.

exam.title: Majority Element II
exam.note: Voting with two candidates (anything above n/3).

exam.title: Rotate Array
exam.note: Reverse all, then reverse both parts.

exam.title: Rotate Image
exam.note: Rotation = transpose + reverse each row.

exam.title: Spiral Matrix
exam.note: Walk the boundary and shrink it four sides at a time.

exam.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
exam.note: Use the first row/column as your marker storage.

exam.title: Valid Sudoku
exam.note: Three families of sets: rows, columns, boxes (box = r//3, c//3).

name: Two Pointers
idea: When the data is sorted or has a direction, two indexes moving with a rule replace a nested loop.
triggers: sorted array + pair/triple → pointers from both ends
"in place", "remove", "compact" → slow writer + fast reader
comparing two sequences → one pointer each
"max area between two lines" → move the weaker side

exam.title: Reverse String
exam.note: Swap ends, move inward. The template.

exam.title: Valid Palindrome
exam.note: Same, but skip characters that are not letters or digits.

exam.title: Squares of a Sorted Array
exam.note: The largest square is at one of the two ends. Fill the answer from the back.

exam.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
exam.note: Sum too small → move left up, too big → move right down. Why is that safe?

exam.title: Valid Palindrome II
exam.note: At the first mismatch, try skipping one side or the other.

exam.title: Remove Element
exam.note: Writer index keeps everything you want to keep.

exam.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
exam.note: Keep x if it differs from the last kept value.

exam.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II
exam.note: Keep x if it differs from the value two slots back in the kept part.

exam.title: Move Zeroes
exam.note: Writer collects non-zeros, then fill the rest with zeros.

exam.title: Merge Sorted Array
exam.note: Merge from the back so you never overwrite unread data.

exam.title: Is Subsequence
exam.note: One pointer per string. Advance the small one only on a match.

exam.title: Append Characters to String to Make Subsequence
exam.note: Same as 392, then count what's left over.

exam.title: 3Sum
exam.note: Fix one number, run 167 on the rest. Skip duplicates at both levels.

exam.title: 3Sum Closest
exam.note: Same as 3Sum, but track the closest sum instead of exact matches.

exam.title: 4Sum
exam.note: One more fixed loop on top of 3Sum. The pattern generalises.

exam.title: Valid Triangle Number
exam.note: Sort, fix the largest side, count pairs with two pointers.

exam.title: Boats to Save People
exam.note: Heaviest person goes with the lightest if they fit.

exam.title: Max Number of K-Sum Pairs
exam.note: Sorted pairs summing to k, or a counting map.

exam.title: Count Pairs Whose Sum is Less than Target
exam.note: Count pairs with sum < target: when it fits, all pairs between the pointers count.

exam.title: Container With Most Water
exam.note: Move the shorter wall. The taller one can't help while the short one limits you.

exam.title: Trapping Rain Water
exam.note: The water at i depends on min(maxLeft, maxRight). Move the side with the smaller max.

exam.title: Sort Colors
exam.note: Three pointers: low zone, unknown zone, high zone (Dutch flag).

exam.title: Next Permutation
exam.note: From the right, find the first dip, swap with the next larger, reverse the tail.

exam.title: Move Pieces to Obtain a String
exam.note: Pieces can only move one way: match the non-blank characters with two pointers.

exam.title: Backspace String Compare
exam.note: Walk both strings from the back, counting backspaces.

exam.title: Interval List Intersections
exam.note: Intersect the current pair, then advance whichever ends first.

exam.title: Long Pressed Name
exam.note: Group runs of each character on both sides.

exam.title: Maximum Distance Between a Pair of Values
exam.note: Pointer per array; widen j while the condition holds.

name: Sliding Window
idea: A contiguous subarray/substring whose condition can be updated in O(1) as you add the right element or drop the left one.
triggers: "contiguous subarray/substring" + longest/shortest/count → window
fixed size k → slide by one
"at most K distinct/zeros/changes" → expand right, shrink left while invalid
"exactly K" → atMost(K) − atMost(K−1)

exam.title: Maximum Average Subarray I
exam.note: Add the new element, drop the old one. Never recompute the sum.

exam.title: Maximum Number of Vowels in a Substring of Given Length
exam.note: Same slide, but you're counting vowels.

exam.title: Number of Sub-arrays of Size K and Average Greater than or Equal to Threshold
exam.note: Fixed window + compare with threshold × k.

exam.title: Minimum Recolors to Get K Consecutive Black Blocks
exam.note: Count the whites in each window of size k.

exam.title: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards
exam.note: Taking from both ends = leaving a middle window of n−k. Minimise that.

exam.title: Find All Anagrams in a String
exam.note: A fixed window of letter counts, compared with the target's counts.

exam.title: Permutation in String
exam.note: The same as 438, but stop at the first match.

exam.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
exam.note: Expand right. While there's a repeat, shrink left. Record the max.

exam.title: Max Consecutive Ones III
exam.note: Valid means "at most k zeros inside". Same expand/shrink loop.

exam.title: Longest Subarray of 1's After Deleting One Element
exam.note: 1004 with k = 1, then subtract the deleted element.

exam.title: Maximize the Confusion of an Exam
exam.note: Run 1004 twice: once treating T as good, once treating F as good.

exam.title: Fruit Into Baskets
exam.note: Valid means "at most 2 distinct types". Needs a count map.

exam.title: Maximum Erasure Value
exam.note: Unique window (like problem 3) but you maximise the sum.

exam.title: Get Equal Substrings Within Budget
exam.note: Valid means "the cost inside ≤ budget".

exam.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
exam.note: Valid means windowLen − maxFreq ≤ k. Why can maxFreq stay stale?

exam.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
exam.note: Shrink while still valid, recording the min each time.

exam.title: Minimum Operations to Reduce X to Zero
exam.note: Removing from both ends = keep the longest middle window with sum total − x.

exam.title: Minimum Window Substring
exam.note: Track how many required characters are satisfied. Shrink while all are.

exam.title: Subarray Product Less Than K
exam.note: Every valid window ending at right adds (right − left + 1) subarrays.

exam.title: Count Subarrays With Score Less Than K
exam.note: Same count trick, with score = sum × length.

exam.title: Number of Substrings Containing All Three Characters
exam.note: Once the window is valid, every extension to the right is valid too.

exam.title: Count Subarrays Where Max Element Appears at Least K Times
exam.note: Count windows with at least k copies of the max element.

exam.title: Binary Subarrays With Sum
exam.note: "Sum exactly goal" is atMost(goal) − atMost(goal−1).

exam.title: Count Number of Nice Subarrays
exam.note: Odd numbers act as 1, evens as 0. Then it's 930.

exam.title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
exam.note: Exactly K distinct = atMost(K) − atMost(K−1).

exam.title: Sliding Window Maximum
exam.note: Monotonic deque: keep candidates in decreasing order.

exam.title: Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Diff Less Than or Equal to Limit
exam.note: Two deques (max and min) so the window knows its range.

exam.title: Maximum Number of Robots Within Budget
exam.note: Deque for the max + running sum for the cost.

exam.title: Sliding Window Median
exam.note: Window median: two heaps or a sorted list with removals.

name: Prefix Sums
idea: Any range total is prefix[r] − prefix[l]. Store prefixes in a map to count ranges with a property.
triggers: many range-sum queries → prefix array
"count subarrays with sum = k" (negatives allowed) → prefix + hashmap
"divisible by k" → prefix mod k
many range updates, one read → difference array
2D sub-rectangle sums → 2D prefix

exam.title: Running Sum of 1d Array
exam.note: Build the prefix array itself.

exam.title: Find the Highest Altitude
exam.note: Running total, track the max.

exam.title: Find Pivot Index
exam.note: Left sum = prefix, right sum = total − prefix − x.

exam.title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
exam.note: Answer each query in O(1) with prefix[r+1] − prefix[l].

exam.title: Left and Right Sum Differences
exam.note: Left sum and right sum for every index.

exam.title: Minimum Value to Get Positive Step by Step Sum
exam.note: Find the lowest point of the prefix sum.

exam.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
exam.note: Count earlier prefixes equal to current − k. Seed the map with {0: 1}.

exam.title: Subarray Sums Divisible by K
exam.note: Same, but the key is prefix mod k (careful with negatives).

exam.title: Continuous Subarray Sum
exam.note: Store the first index of each remainder. You need length ≥ 2.

exam.title: Contiguous Array
exam.note: Turn 0 into −1. Now it's "longest subarray with sum 0".

exam.title: Longest Well-Performing Interval
exam.note: Tiring day = +1, otherwise −1. Longest subarray with positive sum.

exam.title: Count of Interesting Subarrays
exam.note: Mark matches as 1, then count prefix values mod m.

exam.title: Find the Longest Substring Containing Vowels in Even Counts
exam.note: The key is a bitmask of vowel parities.

exam.title: Number of Wonderful Substrings
exam.note: Bitmask parity prefix, allowing one bit to differ.

exam.title: Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable
exam.note: P[r][c] = sum of the rectangle from (0,0). Inclusion–exclusion for queries.

exam.title: Matrix Block Sum
exam.note: Each block query is one 304 query.

exam.title: Number of Submatrices That Sum to Target
exam.note: Fix two rows, squash the columns to 1D, then run 560.

exam.title: Car Pooling
exam.note: +passengers at start, −passengers at end, then a running sum.

exam.title: Corporate Flight Bookings
exam.note: The same as 1094 with bookings.

exam.title: Maximum Population Year
exam.note: Births +1, deaths −1, the max running sum.

exam.title: Shifting Letters II
exam.note: A difference array over shift amounts.

exam.title: XOR Queries of a Subarray
exam.note: Prefix XOR: xor(l..r) = px[r+1] ^ px[l].

exam.title: Sum of All Odd Length Subarrays
exam.note: Prefix sums + count how many odd-length subarrays include each element.

exam.title: Make Sum Divisible by P
exam.note: Remove the shortest subarray so total % p == 0. It's prefix mod + a map of last indexes.

name: Binary Search
idea: If you can say "everything left of here is NO, everything right is YES", you can find the boundary in log time. The array doesn't have to be sorted.
triggers: sorted data → search directly
"min possible max" or "max possible min" → binary search on the answer
rotated/peak/bitonic → compare with mid's neighbour or an end
check(x) is monotonic → search over x

exam.title: Binary Search
exam.note: lo/hi/mid. Decide your loop invariant and stick to it.

exam.title: Search Insert Position
exam.note: Return lo when the loop ends: the first index ≥ target.

exam.title: First Bad Version
exam.note: Find the first true in F F F T T T.

exam.title: Guess Number Higher or Lower
exam.note: Same loop driven by an API.

exam.title: Sqrt(x)
exam.note: Search the answer space 0..x: the biggest m with m·m ≤ x.

exam.title: Valid Perfect Square
exam.note: The same search with an exact check.

exam.title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
exam.note: Two searches: first ≥ target and first > target.

exam.title: Find Smallest Letter Greater Than Target
exam.note: First letter > target, wrap around.

exam.title: Count Negative Numbers in a Sorted Matrix
exam.note: Per row, find the boundary of negatives.

exam.title: Maximum Count of Positive Integer and Negative Integer
exam.note: Count negatives and positives using two boundaries.

exam.title: Peak Index in a Mountain Array
exam.note: Compare mid with mid+1: going up or going down?

exam.title: Find Peak Element
exam.note: The same idea as 852. Some peak always exists in the uphill direction.

exam.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
exam.note: Compare mid with the right end to know which half is sorted.

exam.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
exam.note: Find the sorted half, then check whether target is in it.

exam.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
exam.note: Duplicates break the 153 rule. Shrink hi when equal.

exam.title: Single Element in a Sorted Array
exam.note: Pairs line up on even indexes until the single element appears.

exam.title: Search a 2D Matrix
exam.note: Treat the matrix as one sorted array: index → (i // cols, i % cols).

exam.title: Search a 2D Matrix II
exam.note: Start at the top-right corner: each comparison removes a row or a column.

exam.title: Koko Eating Bananas
exam.note: Guess a speed. Can Koko finish? Faster is always ok, so search the speed.

exam.title: Find the Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold
exam.note: The same shape as Koko with divisors.

exam.title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
exam.note: Guess the capacity, simulate greedily in days.

exam.title: Minimum Number of Days to Make m Bouquets
exam.note: Guess the day, count bouquets that are ready.

exam.title: Maximum Candies Allocated to K Children
exam.note: Guess the pile size, count children served.

exam.title: Minimized Maximum of Products Distributed to Any Store
exam.note: Guess the max per store, count stores needed.

exam.title: Magnetic Force Between Two Balls
exam.note: Max-min: guess the gap, greedily place the balls.

exam.title: Split Array Largest Sum
exam.note: Guess the largest sum, greedily count pieces. (1011 in disguise.)

exam.title: Maximum Number of Removable Characters
exam.note: Guess how many removals, then check the subsequence.

exam.title: Maximum Running Time of N Computers
exam.note: Guess the running time, check total battery ≥ n × time.

exam.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
exam.note: Search on value, count elements ≤ mid with the 240 walk.

exam.title: Kth Smallest Number in Multiplication Table
exam.note: Count numbers ≤ mid in the multiplication table: row by row.

exam.title: Find K-th Smallest Pair Distance
exam.note: Search on distance, count pairs with a sliding window.

exam.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
exam.note: Binary search on the partition of the smaller array.

name: Stack & Monotonic Stack
idea: A stack remembers the unfinished things, latest first. A monotonic stack keeps only candidates that could still be someone's answer.
triggers: matching brackets / undo → stack
"next greater/smaller element" → monotonic stack
nested structure like 3[a2[c]] → stack of states
"largest rectangle", "sum of subarray minimums" → for each element, how far does it reach left and right

exam.title: Valid Parentheses
exam.note: Push openers, pop on closers. Top must match.

exam.title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates In String
exam.note: The stack is the answer: push, or pop if equal to the top.

exam.title: Removing Stars From a String
exam.note: Star = pop.

exam.title: Make The String Great
exam.note: Pop when the top is the same letter in the other case.

exam.title: Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid
exam.note: Count unmatched openers and closers.

exam.title: Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
exam.note: Remember the indexes of unmatched brackets, then delete them.

exam.title: Min Stack
exam.note: Store (value, min so far) on each level.

exam.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
exam.note: Numbers push. Operators pop two and push the result.

exam.title: Simplify Path
exam.note: Split by "/", ".." pops, "." is ignored.

exam.title: Asteroid Collision
exam.note: Collide while the top moves right and the new one moves left.

exam.title: Decode String
exam.note: Push (current string, repeat count) when you see "[". Pop on "]".

exam.title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates in String II
exam.note: Store (char, count) on the stack.

exam.title: Score of Parentheses
exam.note: Push a 0 for each level. On ")", score this level and add it to the parent.

exam.title: Next Greater Element I
exam.note: Pop smaller elements: the new element is their next greater.

exam.title: Daily Temperatures
exam.note: The same, storing indexes to compute the distance.

exam.title: Next Greater Element II
exam.note: Circular: loop twice over the array.

exam.title: Final Prices With a Special Discount in a Shop
exam.note: Next smaller-or-equal element to the right.

exam.title: Online Stock Span
exam.note: Store (price, span) and merge popped spans.

exam.title: Car Fleet
exam.note: Sort by position. A slower car ahead blocks the cars behind it.

exam.title: Remove K Digits
exam.note: Keep the stack increasing, pop while you still have deletions.

exam.title: Remove Duplicate Letters
exam.note: Like 402, but you can only pop a letter if it appears again later.

exam.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
exam.note: For each bar: how far can it extend left and right? Monotonic stack finds both.

exam.title: Maximal Rectangle
exam.note: Each row is a histogram. Run 84 per row.

exam.title: Sum of Subarray Minimums
exam.note: Each element is the minimum of (left reach × right reach) subarrays.

exam.title: Sum of Subarray Ranges
exam.note: Sum of maxima − sum of minima, both with 907's technique.

exam.title: 132 Pattern
exam.note: Scan from the right keeping the best "2" with a stack.

exam.title: Basic Calculator II
exam.note: Apply × and ÷ immediately, push + and − terms.

exam.title: Basic Calculator
exam.note: Parentheses: push the running result and sign, pop on ")".

name: Linked List
idea: Pointers instead of indexes. Most problems are "keep the right references before you overwrite one".
triggers: middle / cycle / nth from end → slow & fast pointers
reverse a part → three pointers prev/cur/next
building a new list → dummy head
O(1) access by key + order → hashmap + doubly linked list

exam.title: Reverse Linked List
exam.note: prev / cur / next. Draw it on paper first.

exam.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
exam.note: A dummy head removes the "which list starts?" special case.

exam.title: Remove Linked List Elements
exam.note: A dummy head again, so you can delete the first node too.

exam.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List
exam.note: Skip next while it has the same value.

exam.title: Middle of the Linked List
exam.note: Slow moves 1, fast moves 2. When fast ends, slow is in the middle.

exam.title: Linked List Cycle
exam.note: Slow and fast meet if there is a cycle.

exam.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
exam.note: Move fast n steps ahead, then move both together.

exam.title: Delete the Middle Node of a Linked List
exam.note: Middle-finding with one step of delay, then delete.

exam.title: Intersection of Two Linked Lists
exam.note: Each pointer walks A then B, so both travel the same total length.

exam.title: Linked List Cycle II
exam.note: After they meet, restart one at the head: they meet again at the cycle start.

exam.title: Palindrome Linked List
exam.note: Find the middle, reverse the second half, compare.

exam.title: Odd Even Linked List
exam.note: Two chains (odd, even) and join them.

exam.title: Reverse Linked List II
exam.note: Reverse only positions left..right. Keep the node before the range.

exam.title: Swap Nodes in Pairs
exam.note: Swap in pairs using a dummy head.

exam.title: Rotate List
exam.note: Make it a ring, then cut at the right place.

exam.title: Partition List
exam.note: Two dummy lists: less than x and the rest.

exam.title: Reorder List
exam.note: Middle + reverse + merge alternately. Three skills combined.

exam.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II
exam.note: Skip whole runs of duplicates using a dummy head.

exam.title: Add Two Numbers
exam.note: Add digit by digit with a carry.

exam.title: Add Two Numbers II
exam.note: Same addition, but digits are reversed: use stacks or reverse first.

exam.title: Copy List with Random Pointer
exam.note: Map old nodes to new ones, or interleave copies in the list.

exam.title: LRU Cache
exam.note: Hashmap for lookup + doubly linked list for recency order.

exam.title: Sort List
exam.note: Merge sort on a list: middle + sort halves + merge (21).

exam.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
exam.note: Merge k lists with a min-heap, or merge pairs repeatedly.

exam.title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
exam.note: Reverse k nodes at a time, link groups, keep the rest if shorter.

name: Trees
idea: Most tree problems are: "what do I need from my left child and my right child to answer for myself?"
triggers: anything about every root-to-leaf path → DFS carrying state down
depth, height, diameter → DFS returning info up
per level / nearest → BFS with a queue
BST → inorder is sorted, go left or right
distance between nodes → treat the tree as a graph

exam.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
exam.note: depth(node) = 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)).

exam.title: Invert Binary Tree
exam.note: Swap children, recurse.

exam.title: Same Tree
exam.note: Compare the two trees node by node.

exam.title: Symmetric Tree
exam.note: Is the left subtree a mirror of the right? A helper with two arguments.

exam.title: Minimum Depth of Binary Tree
exam.note: Careful: a node with one child is not a leaf.

exam.title: Path Sum
exam.note: Pass the remaining sum down.

exam.title: Balanced Binary Tree
exam.note: Return the height, or −1 to mean "already unbalanced".

exam.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
exam.note: At each node, longest path = left height + right height. The answer is not what you return.

exam.title: Subtree of Another Tree
exam.note: For each node, run "same tree" (100).

exam.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
exam.note: Queue, and process exactly len(queue) nodes per level.

exam.title: Average of Levels in Binary Tree
exam.note: The same loop, average each level.

exam.title: Find Largest Value in Each Tree Row
exam.note: The same loop, max of each level.

exam.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
exam.note: The last node of each level.

exam.title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
exam.note: Level order, reversing every other level.

exam.title: Maximum Level Sum of a Binary Tree
exam.note: Sum per level, keep the best.

exam.title: Maximum Width of Binary Tree
exam.note: Give nodes position indexes like a heap: 2i and 2i+1.

exam.title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
exam.note: Pass the max so far down the path.

exam.title: Sum Root to Leaf Numbers
exam.note: Pass the number built so far down.

exam.title: Path Sum II
exam.note: Backtracking on a tree: push, recurse, pop.

exam.title: Path Sum III
exam.note: Prefix sums along the current path (560 on a tree).

exam.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
exam.note: If p and q come from different sides, this node is the LCA.

exam.title: Longest ZigZag Path in a Binary Tree
exam.note: Return the zigzag length for both directions.

exam.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
exam.note: Return the best one-sided path. Update the answer with both sides.

exam.title: Search in a Binary Search Tree
exam.note: Go left or right. No need to visit both.

exam.title: Insert into a Binary Search Tree
exam.note: Walk down to the empty spot.

exam.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
exam.note: Pass a (low, high) range down.

exam.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
exam.note: Inorder traversal visits values in sorted order.

exam.title: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree
exam.note: The middle element becomes the root.

exam.title: Delete Node in a BST
exam.note: Three cases: no child, one child, two children (use the successor).

exam.title: Binary Search Tree Iterator
exam.note: Inorder traversal with your own stack, one step at a time.

exam.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
exam.note: Preorder gives the root, inorder splits left and right.

exam.title: Construct Binary Tree from Inorder and Postorder Traversal
exam.note: The same with postorder (root is at the end).

exam.title: Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List
exam.note: Flatten: preorder order using right pointers.

exam.title: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node
exam.note: Use the level you've already linked to link the next one.

exam.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
exam.note: Preorder with null markers, then rebuild recursively.

exam.title: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree
exam.note: Add parent links, then BFS from the target.

exam.title: Amount of Time for Binary Tree to Be Infected
exam.note: The same as 863: tree → graph, then BFS.

exam.title: Binary Tree Cameras
exam.note: Each node returns a state: covered / has camera / needs cover.

name: Heaps / Priority Queue
idea: When you repeatedly need "the current best" while things are added and removed, a heap gives it in log time.
triggers: k largest / k smallest / k closest → heap of size k
repeatedly take max and modify → max-heap simulation
median of a stream → two heaps
merge k sorted things → heap of heads
schedule by time, pick best available → sort by time + heap

exam.title: Last Stone Weight
exam.note: Simulate with a max-heap: pop two, push the difference.

exam.title: Take Gifts From the Richest Pile
exam.note: Pop the max, push sqrt, k times.

exam.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
exam.note: Keep a min-heap of size k: its top is the kth largest.

exam.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
exam.note: The same size-k heap (or quickselect).

exam.title: K Closest Points to Origin
exam.note: Max-heap of size k by distance.

exam.title: Remove Stones to Minimize the Total
exam.note: Greedily halve the largest pile.

exam.title: Reorganize String
exam.note: Always place the most frequent char that isn't the last one placed.

exam.title: Longest Happy String
exam.note: The same idea with a limit of two in a row.

exam.title: Task Scheduler
exam.note: Most frequent tasks first, with idle slots (or the formula).

exam.title: Minimum Operations to Halve Array Sum
exam.note: Always halve the current largest number: a max-heap greedy.

exam.title: Find Median from Data Stream
exam.note: Max-heap for the lower half, min-heap for the upper half, balance sizes.

exam.title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
exam.note: Start with (i, 0) pairs, push the next j when you pop.

exam.title: Minimize Deviation in Array
exam.note: Make all numbers even-max, then shrink the max with a heap.

exam.title: Single-Threaded CPU
exam.note: Sort by arrival. Add arrived tasks to the heap, pick the shortest.

exam.title: Meeting Rooms III
exam.note: Two heaps: free rooms by number, busy rooms by end time.

exam.title: Furthest Building You Can Reach
exam.note: Use ladders on the biggest climbs: a min-heap of ladder climbs.

exam.title: Minimum Number of Refueling Stops
exam.note: Pass stations, and only "refuel" from the biggest you've passed when needed.

exam.title: IPO
exam.note: Sort by capital. Unlock projects, take the best profit.

exam.title: Course Schedule III
exam.note: Sort by deadline. If over time, drop the longest course taken.

exam.title: Maximum Subsequence Score
exam.note: Sort by the multiplier, keep the k largest sums with a heap.

exam.title: Minimum Cost to Hire K Workers
exam.note: Sort by wage/quality ratio, keep the k smallest qualities.

name: Backtracking
idea: Build a choice step by step, undo it, try the next. The skill is drawing the decision tree first.
triggers: "all subsets/combinations/permutations" → backtracking
n ≤ ~15 and "every way" → try everything with pruning
grid word path → DFS with visited marks undone after
duplicates in input → sort + skip equal siblings

exam.title: Subsets
exam.note: At each index: take it or skip it. That's the whole tree.

exam.title: Subsets II
exam.note: Sort, then skip equal values at the same tree level.

exam.title: Sum of All Subset XOR Totals
exam.note: Subsets again, but carry the XOR.

exam.title: Combinations
exam.note: Choose k from n: start each level from the next number.

exam.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
exam.note: One level per digit, branch over its letters.

exam.title: Combination Sum
exam.note: You may reuse a number: recurse from the same index.

exam.title: Combination Sum II
exam.note: No reuse + duplicates: 90's skip rule with a target.

exam.title: Combination Sum III
exam.note: Fixed count k and target sum together.

exam.title: Permutations
exam.note: A used[] array: each level picks any unused number.

exam.title: Permutations II
exam.note: Sort + skip a value if the same value before it is unused.

exam.title: Generate Parentheses
exam.note: Add "(" while opens < n, add ")" while closes < opens.

exam.title: Palindrome Partitioning
exam.note: At each start index, try every palindromic prefix.

exam.title: Restore IP Addresses
exam.note: Each level takes 1–3 digits, and must be a valid octet.

exam.title: Word Search
exam.note: Grid DFS: mark visited, recurse, unmark.

exam.title: Path with Maximum Gold
exam.note: 79 again, but you maximise the gold collected.

exam.title: Fair Distribution of Cookies
exam.note: Give each cookie bag to some child. Prune with the current best.

exam.title: N-Queens
exam.note: Place one queen per row. Track columns and both diagonals.

exam.title: N-Queens II
exam.note: The same search, but count.

exam.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
exam.note: Fill k buckets one at a time. Sort descending and prune hard.

exam.title: Matchsticks to Square
exam.note: 698 with k = 4.

exam.title: Sudoku Solver
exam.note: Try digits in empty cells with row/column/box sets.

exam.title: Word Search II
exam.note: Word Search with a trie so all words are searched at once.

name: Graphs: BFS & DFS
idea: A grid or a list of connections is a graph. DFS explores everything connected. BFS explores in distance order, so it finds shortest paths when every step costs 1.
triggers: islands / regions / connected parts → DFS or BFS flood fill
minimum steps, each step costs 1 → BFS
spreading from many sources at once → multi-source BFS
"is it possible to split into two groups" → bipartite colouring
state = position + extra info → BFS over (position, info)

exam.title: Flood Fill
exam.note: DFS from one cell, change matching neighbours.

exam.title: Number of Islands
exam.note: For each unvisited land cell: count it and flood the whole island.

exam.title: Max Area of Island
exam.note: The same, but return the size from the flood.

exam.title: Island Perimeter
exam.note: Count edges that touch water or the border.

exam.title: Number of Enclaves
exam.note: Flood from the border first, then count what's left.

exam.title: Number of Closed Islands
exam.note: The same border trick: islands touching the border don't count.

exam.title: Surrounded Regions
exam.note: Mark border-connected O's as safe, flip the rest.

exam.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
exam.note: Flood backwards from each ocean, then intersect.

exam.title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
exam.note: Build an adjacency list, then DFS/BFS from the source.

exam.title: Find the Town Judge
exam.note: In-degree and out-degree are enough. No traversal needed.

exam.title: Keys and Rooms
exam.note: DFS from room 0 and check everything was visited.

exam.title: Number of Provinces
exam.note: Count connected components.

exam.title: Reorder Routes to Make All Paths Lead to the City Zero
exam.note: Store edge directions, count edges pointing away from 0.

exam.title: Clone Graph
exam.note: Map old node → new node while you DFS.

exam.title: Rotting Oranges
exam.note: Multi-source BFS: start the queue with all rotten oranges.

exam.title: 01 Matrix
exam.note: Multi-source BFS from all zeros.

exam.title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
exam.note: BFS on a grid with 8 directions.

exam.title: Nearest Exit from Entrance in Maze
exam.note: BFS until you reach a border cell.

exam.title: Open the Lock
exam.note: Each state is a 4-digit string. Neighbours turn one wheel.

exam.title: Minimum Genetic Mutation
exam.note: The same as 752 with genes.

exam.title: Word Ladder
exam.note: The same shape with words. Use wildcard keys to find neighbours fast.

exam.title: Snakes and Ladders
exam.note: Turn the board into numbers, then BFS over squares.

exam.title: Is Graph Bipartite?
exam.note: Colour with BFS: a neighbour with the same colour means not bipartite.

exam.title: Possible Bipartition
exam.note: Build the graph from dislikes, then run 785.

exam.title: Find Eventual Safe States
exam.note: Safe = cannot reach a cycle. Use 3 colours or reverse topological order.

exam.title: Shortest Path in a Grid with Obstacles Elimination
exam.note: The state is (row, col, removals left).

exam.title: Shortest Path to Get All Keys
exam.note: The state is (row, col, keys held as a bitmask).

exam.title: Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes
exam.note: The state is (node, set of visited nodes as a bitmask).

name: Topological Sort, Union-Find, Dijkstra
idea: Three graph tools: order things with dependencies, merge groups quickly, find cheapest paths when steps have different costs.
triggers: prerequisites / "order of tasks" → topological sort
"are these connected?" with edges added over time → union-find
weighted shortest path → Dijkstra
cheapest network connecting everything → minimum spanning tree

exam.title: Course Schedule
exam.note: Kahn's algorithm: repeatedly take nodes with in-degree 0. Leftovers mean a cycle.

exam.title: Course Schedule II
exam.note: The same, and record the order.

exam.title: Find All Possible Recipes from Given Supplies
exam.note: Recipes depend on ingredients. Topological sort on names.

exam.title: Course Schedule IV
exam.note: Topological order + propagate "reachable" sets.

exam.title: Minimum Height Trees
exam.note: Peel leaves layer by layer. The last layer is the answer.

exam.title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
exam.note: DFS with memo on the grid. Increasing paths form a DAG.

exam.title: Redundant Connection
exam.note: Add edges one by one: the first one joining an existing group is the answer.

exam.title: Number of Operations to Make Network Connected
exam.note: Components − 1 cables needed, if there are enough cables.

exam.title: Satisfiability of Equality Equations
exam.note: Union all "==" first, then check "!=".

exam.title: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column
exam.note: Union stones in the same row or column. Answer = stones − groups.

exam.title: Accounts Merge
exam.note: Union accounts that share an email.

exam.title: Smallest String With Swaps
exam.note: Union swappable indexes, sort the characters inside each group.

exam.title: Network Delay Time
exam.note: The template: a min-heap of (distance, node).

exam.title: Path with Maximum Probability
exam.note: Maximise probability: a max-heap version.

exam.title: Path With Minimum Effort
exam.note: The path cost is the max step, not the sum. Dijkstra still works.

exam.title: Swim in Rising Water
exam.note: The same shape as 1631 with time.

exam.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
exam.note: At most k stops: Bellman-Ford with k+1 rounds.

exam.title: Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination
exam.note: Dijkstra + count the ways to reach each node at its best distance.

exam.title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
exam.note: Connect all points cheaply: Prim's or Kruskal's.

exam.title: Find Critical and Pseudo-Critical Edges in Minimum Spanning Tree
exam.note: Run Kruskal's with an edge forced in or left out.

exam.title: Evaluate Division
exam.note: A weighted graph of ratios. DFS multiplies along the path.

exam.title: Reconstruct Itinerary
exam.note: Eulerian path: Hierholzer's algorithm with sorted neighbours.

exam.title: Critical Connections in a Network
exam.note: Bridges: Tarjan's low-link values.

name: Greedy & Intervals
idea: Make the locally best choice, but only after you can explain why it never hurts. Intervals almost always start with sorting.
triggers: overlapping intervals → sort by start (merge) or by end (choose the most)
"minimum number of jumps/steps" → track the farthest reach
pick a subset that maximises something → sort by the deciding attribute
"max subarray sum" → Kadane

exam.title: Assign Cookies
exam.note: Sort both. Give the smallest cookie that satisfies the least greedy child.

exam.title: Lemonade Change
exam.note: Give change with the biggest bills first.

exam.title: Can Place Flowers
exam.note: Plant whenever both neighbours are empty.

exam.title: Maximize Sum Of Array After K Negations
exam.note: Flip the most negative numbers first.

exam.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
exam.note: Track the lowest price so far.

exam.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
exam.note: Take every upward step.

exam.title: Jump Game
exam.note: Track the farthest index you can reach.

exam.title: Jump Game II
exam.note: BFS by levels: each jump covers the range reachable from the current one.

exam.title: Gas Station
exam.note: If the tank goes negative, the start must be after this point.

exam.title: Hand of Straights
exam.note: Always start a group at the smallest card left.

exam.title: Valid Parenthesis String
exam.note: Track the range of possible open-bracket counts.

exam.title: Candy
exam.note: Two passes: left-to-right, then right-to-left.

exam.title: Merge Intervals
exam.note: Sort by start, extend the last merged interval or start a new one.

exam.title: Insert Interval
exam.note: Add the ones before, merge the overlapping ones, add the rest.

exam.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
exam.note: Sort by end. Keep the interval that ends first.

exam.title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
exam.note: The same as 435: arrows = intervals you keep.

exam.title: Remove Covered Intervals
exam.note: Sort by start ascending, end descending.

exam.title: Divide Intervals Into Minimum Number of Groups
exam.note: Groups = the max number of intervals overlapping at once.

exam.title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
exam.note: Sort queries and intervals, use a heap of interval sizes.

exam.title: Partition Labels
exam.note: The last occurrence of each letter decides where a part can end.

exam.title: Maximum Subarray
exam.note: Kadane: drop the running sum when it goes negative.

exam.title: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray
exam.note: Circular = total − minimum subarray (careful when all negative).

exam.title: Two City Scheduling
exam.note: Sort by the cost difference between the two cities.

exam.title: Dota2 Senate
exam.note: Two queues of indexes: the earlier senator bans the other.

name: Dynamic Programming (1D)
idea: If the answer for n is built from answers for smaller n, write the recurrence, then fill a table. The hard part is choosing what dp[i] means.
triggers: "number of ways" → DP
"min/max cost to reach the end" → DP
take or skip each item → DP over index
coins/items reusable → unbounded knapsack
each item once with a sum target → 0/1 knapsack
"longest increasing subsequence" → LIS

exam.title: Fibonacci Number
exam.note: dp[i] = dp[i−1] + dp[i−2]. Then do it with two variables.

exam.title: Climbing Stairs
exam.note: The same recurrence: the last step was 1 or 2.

exam.title: N-th Tribonacci Number
exam.note: Three previous values instead of two.

exam.title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
exam.note: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i−1], dp[i−2]).

exam.title: House Robber
exam.note: Rob house i or skip it: dp[i] = max(dp[i−1], dp[i−2] + nums[i]).

exam.title: House Robber II
exam.note: Circular: run 198 twice, without the first or without the last.

exam.title: Delete and Earn
exam.note: Group equal values, then it's House Robber on values.

exam.title: Decode Ways
exam.note: dp[i] = ways for the first i characters: one-digit and two-digit last pieces.

exam.title: Word Break
exam.note: dp[i] = can the first i characters be split? Try every last word.

exam.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
exam.note: Expand around each centre, or dp[i][j] = is s[i..j] a palindrome.

exam.title: Palindromic Substrings
exam.note: The same centres, but count.

exam.title: Coin Change
exam.note: Unbounded: dp[a] = 1 + min over coins of dp[a − coin].

exam.title: Perfect Squares
exam.note: The same as 322 with squares as coins.

exam.title: Coin Change 2
exam.note: Count combinations: loop coins on the outside.

exam.title: Combination Sum IV
exam.note: Count orderings: loop amounts on the outside. Compare with 518!

exam.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
exam.note: 0/1 knapsack: can a subset reach total / 2? Loop the sum backwards.

exam.title: Target Sum
exam.note: Turn +/− into "subset sum = (total + target) / 2".

exam.title: Last Stone Weight II
exam.note: The same split-into-two-halves as 416.

exam.title: Ones and Zeroes
exam.note: A knapsack with two capacities (zeros and ones).

exam.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
exam.note: dp[i] = LIS ending at i. Then the O(n log n) version with binary search.

exam.title: Number of Longest Increasing Subsequence
exam.note: Track the length and the count at each index.

exam.title: Largest Divisible Subset
exam.note: Sort, then LIS where "divides" replaces "less than".

exam.title: Russian Doll Envelopes
exam.note: Sort by width (and height descending on ties), then LIS on heights.

exam.title: Find the Longest Valid Obstacle Course at Each Position
exam.note: LIS with "≤", with binary search for every prefix.

exam.title: Maximum Product Subarray
exam.note: Track both the max and the min ending here (a negative flips them).

exam.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
exam.note: States: holding, sold today (cooldown), resting.

exam.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Transaction Fee
exam.note: Two states, subtract the fee on a sale.

exam.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III
exam.note: Four states: buy1, sell1, buy2, sell2.

exam.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock IV
exam.note: Generalise 123 to k transactions.

name: Dynamic Programming (2D)
idea: When the state needs two numbers (two positions, a range i..j, a position + a count), the table becomes 2D. Same rules: define dp, recurrence, order of filling.
triggers: grid paths → dp[r][c] from top/left
two strings compared → dp[i][j] over prefixes
substring/range of one string → interval dp[i][j]
"burst / cut / merge in some order" → interval DP picking the last action
small n (≤ 20) with subsets → bitmask DP

exam.title: Unique Paths II
exam.note: The same with blocked cells set to 0.

exam.title: Minimum Path Sum
exam.note: min instead of +, plus the cell's cost.

exam.title: Triangle
exam.note: Go from the bottom row up.

exam.title: Minimum Falling Path Sum
exam.note: Three cells from the row above.

exam.title: Maximal Square
exam.note: The square ending here = 1 + min(top, left, top-left).

exam.title: Longest Common Subsequence
exam.note: LCS: match → diagonal + 1, otherwise max(top, left). The parent of the whole family.

exam.title: Delete Operation for Two Strings
exam.note: Deletions = len1 + len2 − 2 × LCS.

exam.title: Minimum ASCII Delete Sum for Two Strings
exam.note: The same as 583, but weighted by ASCII values.

exam.title: Edit Distance
exam.note: Edit distance: insert / delete / replace = three neighbours.

exam.title: Interleaving String
exam.note: dp[i][j] = can the first i of s1 and j of s2 make the first i+j of s3?

exam.title: Distinct Subsequences
exam.note: Count ways: match → use it or skip it.

exam.title: Shortest Common Supersequence
exam.note: Build LCS, then walk the table to construct the answer.

exam.title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
exam.note: dp[i][j] over the range: ends match → inside + 2.

exam.title: Minimum Insertion Steps to Make a String Palindrome
exam.note: Insertions = n − longest palindromic subsequence.

exam.title: Minimum Score Triangulation of Polygon
exam.note: Choose the triangle on edge (i, j): split into two smaller polygons.

exam.title: Guess Number Higher or Lower II
exam.note: Pick the guess k in the range, pay k + the worse side.

exam.title: Burst Balloons
exam.note: Choose which balloon bursts last in (i, j).

exam.title: Minimum Cost to Cut a Stick
exam.note: The same "choose the last cut" structure as 312.

exam.title: Regular Expression Matching
exam.note: "*" means zero copies (skip two) or one more copy (stay).

exam.title: Wildcard Matching
exam.note: "*" matches empty (skip) or one more char (stay).

exam.title: House Robber III
exam.note: Tree DP: return (rob this node, skip this node).

exam.title: Minimum Number of Work Sessions to Finish the Tasks
exam.note: Bitmask DP over which tasks are done.

exam.title: Parallel Courses II
exam.note: Bitmask DP over courses taken (with prerequisites).

name: Bit Manipulation
idea: Numbers are bit arrays. XOR cancels pairs, AND checks bits, shifts multiply or divide by two.
triggers: "every element appears twice except one" → XOR everything
count set bits → n & (n−1) removes the lowest one
subsets of a small set → bitmask
maximise XOR → greedily from the highest bit (often with a trie)

exam.title: Number of 1 Bits
exam.note: n & (n−1) drops the lowest set bit. Count how many times.

exam.title: Power of Two
exam.note: A power of two has exactly one set bit.

exam.title: Counting Bits
exam.note: bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1).

exam.title: Reverse Bits
exam.note: Shift bits out of n into the result.

exam.title: Single Number
exam.note: XOR everything: pairs cancel out.

exam.title: Missing Number
exam.note: XOR the indexes with the values.

exam.title: Find The Original Array of Prefix Xor
exam.note: prefix[i] ^ prefix[i−1] gives the original array.

exam.title: Minimum Flips to Make a OR b Equal to c
exam.note: Check bit by bit what flips are needed.

exam.title: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range
exam.note: The answer is the common prefix of left and right.

exam.title: Sum of Two Integers
exam.note: Sum without +: XOR for sum, AND+shift for carry.

exam.title: Single Number II
exam.note: Count each bit position mod 3.

exam.title: Single Number III
exam.note: XOR all, split by any set bit, XOR each group.

exam.title: Largest Combination With Bitwise AND Greater Than Zero
exam.note: The best bit position: count how many numbers have it.

exam.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
exam.note: Build the answer greedily from the top bit with a set or trie.

name: Trie
idea: A tree of characters, so many words that share prefixes share storage, and prefix questions take O(word length).
triggers: "starts with" / autocomplete → trie
search many words in a grid → trie + DFS
replace with the shortest root → trie walk
max XOR pair → binary trie

exam.title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
exam.note: Each node: children + an end-of-word flag.

exam.title: Longest Common Prefix
exam.note: Walk the trie while there's only one child (or just compare strings).

exam.title: Longest Word in Dictionary
exam.note: Build the trie, then DFS only through end-of-word nodes.

exam.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
exam.note: "." means try every child: DFS on the trie.

exam.title: Replace Words
exam.note: Walk each word until you hit the first end-of-word flag.

exam.title: Search Suggestions System
exam.note: Sort the words, or store the top 3 at each trie node.

exam.title: Map Sum Pairs
exam.note: Store sums at each node along the path.

exam.title: Word Search II
exam.note: Build the trie of words, DFS the grid along trie edges.

exam.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
exam.note: A binary trie: for each number, walk the opposite bit when possible.

exam.title: Maximum XOR With an Element From Array
exam.note: Sort queries offline, insert numbers ≤ limit, then 421.

exam.title: Palindrome Pairs
exam.note: For each word, look up reversed pieces that form a palindrome.
